title: Quantization and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Alicia Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook documents the integrated process we use at Redwood Inference for: (1) model onboarding into the eval harness, (2) standardized prompt sets and benchmarks, (3) defining quality guardrails, (4) producing recommended quantization profiles, and (5) a repeatable regression triage workflow when quality or performance regressions are observed. This is intended for applied ML engineers, model owners, and SREs who operate inference at scale.

Goals

- Reduce time-to-safe-deployment for new model variants to <= 2 business days for routine cases.
- Ensure quantization recommendations meet target throughput uplift goals while keeping quality delta <= 2% for benchmark metrics.
- Provide a deterministic, documented regression triage that reaches a root-cause hypothesis within 48 hours for P1/P2 regressions.

Scope

This playbook covers: experimental and production model onboarding, benchmark creation & maintenance, quantization profile evaluation, and escalation/triage steps for quality and perf regressions. It does not cover customer-specific legal/compliance reviews (see security-and-compliance).

Ownership and Roles

- Model Owner: single person responsible for onboarding, tuning, and final signoff.
- Eval Lead (Applied ML): owns eval harness integration, benchmark maintenance, and baseline metrics.
- Quantization SME (Serving Runtime): produces quant profiles, runs microbenchmarks on runtime.
- SRE / Performance Owner: validates throughput/SLO impact in staging, coordinates capacity.
- Incident Lead (for regressions): triage owner who coordinates cross-team investigation.

Each onboarded model must include an explicit Owner and an Eval Lead assigned in the model metadata.

Eval Harness Integration (step-by-step)

1) Prepare model artifacts
   - Provide model weights (s3 or internal blob storage) and model card with architecture, tokenizer, and training data tags.
   - Include a minimal inference example in Python and a model configuration (JSON) describing max sequence length, supported batch sizes, kv-cache compatibility, and recommended precision formats.

2) Add to Eval Harness
   - Create a new entry in the eval-harness catalog: eval_harness/catalog/<model-name>.yaml (use template).
   - Add deterministic unit tests: small prompt -> expected token prefix (where applicable) and shape tests for embeddings.
   - Register model config with evaluation CI; make sure the model can be loaded in the harness container image used by CI.

3) Baseline runs
   - Run the standard benchmark suite (see Prompt Sets and Benchmarks) with N=3 seeds for sampling-based tasks.
   - Capture metrics: accuracy/EM, BLEU/ROUGE (as relevant), factuality score (if available), toxicity check, latency P50/P95, tokens/sec.
   - Upload baseline artifacts to model registry and link them in the model card.

Prompt Sets and Benchmarks

Policy:
- Every model must be evaluated with the company-standard prompt sets for: summarization, instruction-following, code generation, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and embeddings similarity.
- Prompt sets are versioned; benchmark results must include the prompt-set version used and any modifications.

Benchmark contents (high-level):
- Unit tasks: short deterministic prompts used for regression detection.
- Macro tasks: longer contextual prompts for latency and throughput characterization.
- Adversarial tasks: targeted prompts for safety/toxicity checks.

Example benchmark metadata block (to include in results):
- prompt_set_version: v2026-02-01
- seed_count: 3
- temperature: 0.2 (unless testing sampling behaviors)

Quality Guardrails

Guardrails we enforce before approving models for production: 
- Metric thresholds: the model's primary metric (defined by product owner per use-case) must not degrade by >1.5% relative to the current production baseline for that use-case. For user-facing instruction tasks we use Exact Match / Instruction Score; for embeddings we use Recall@k/Avg cosine similarity.
- Safety thresholds: toxicity score <= 0.02 (measured with our safety classifier), and the rate of hallucinations (as measured by fact-checker probe suite) must be <= 3%.
- Latency SLO: end-to-end P95 generation latency must be under 800ms for standard small prompts on Hosted instances; Dedicated SLAs may differ—see service runbooks.
- Cost guardrail: per-token cost increase must be justified; any >10% increase requires separate finance approval.

If any guardrail is violated during canary or staged rollout, the model must be rolled back and a root-cause investigation initiated.

Quantization Profiles (workflow and example table)

Workflow:
1) Select candidate quantizations (e.g., fp16, int8, gptq-4bit, awq).
2) For each candidate, generate a quantized model artifact and run the microbenchmark suite on representative hardware (A100, H100, and CPU baseline if relevant).
3) Capture quality delta on the standard prompt sets and measured throughput improvements.
4) Approve quant profile if quality delta <= 2% for the model's primary metric and throughput/efficiency gains meet target.

Recommended starting profiles (subject to model family testing):
| model_family | quant_profile | expected_tokens_per_sec_uplift | typical_quality_delta | notes |
|--------------|---------------|-------------------------------:|---------------------:|-------|
| LlamaX-7B    | gptq-4bit     | 1.9x                          | 0.5%                 | Good balance, test for long-context drift |
| LlamaX-13B   | awq-4bit      | 2.3x                          | 1.2%                 | Monitor rare tokenization edge cases |
| OpenFamily-30B | int8         | 2.8x                          | 2.1%                 | Requires longer eval; may degrade on code tasks |
| Mistral-7B   | fp16          | 1.1x                          | 0.1%                 | Minimal change, lower memory savings |

Notes on table: these are starting recommendations. Quantization SME must produce per-model profiles and attach a parquet/CSV of per-prompt deltas to the model registry.

Regression Triage Playbook (P1/P2 regression)

Triggering events:
- Canary/staging monitors detect a metric regression beyond thresholds (see Quality Guardrails).
- Customer report with reproducible steps that shows a regression.
- Automated eval harness alerts (unit test failures / deterministic prompts changed).

Immediate steps (first 4 hours):
1) Incident lead ack and assemble team (Model Owner, Eval Lead, Quant SME, SRE).
2) Reproduce the regression in a controlled environment using the same prompt set and seeds. Document exact model version, quant profile, and runtime kernel/driver versions.
3) Snapshot artifacts: model config, quantized binaries, eval harness logs, token-level diffs for failing prompts.

Investigation steps (4–24 hours):
1) Isolate variable changes: was there a model version change, quantization profile change, runtime upgrade (driver/CUDA/torch/llama-cpp), or prompt-set change?
2) If quantization is implicated, run a dequantized (fp16) baseline comparison and measure per-prompt deltas to localize failure modes.
3) Perform A/B tests between the last-known-good and current artifacts to measure exact delta distributions.
4) Check infra signals: GPU memory errors, out-of-order kernel scheduling, batching-induced token truncation, or tokenization mismatches.

Resolution & Postmortem (24–72 hours):
- If root cause is quantization: roll back to previous quant profile or deploy fp16 variant; update quantization tests to include the failing prompt examples.
- If root cause is model quality regression: rollback deploy, mark model as blocked in registry, schedule remediation (fine-tuning or prompt engineering).
- If root cause is runtime/kernel: coordinate with serving-runtime team to publish a hotfix and run end-to-end validation.

Deliverables:
- Short incident summary (published to oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems).
- Test-case bundle with failing prompts added to unit regression suite.
- Updated quantization profile if a safe alternative is available.
- Lessons learned and follow-up action items assigned with owners and due dates.

Checklist for Safe Canary/Production Rollout

- [ ] Eval harness baseline results attached to model card.
- [ ] Quantization profile tested and CSV of prompt deltas uploaded.
- [ ] Safety checks (toxicity/fact-check) pass thresholds.
- [ ] Performance verified on staging with load tests: P50/P95 reported.
- [ ] Runbook for rollback prepared and tested.
- [ ] Model Owner and SRE alias included on rollout notification.

Appendix: Useful Commands and Snippets

- Run harness benchmark: python -m eval_harness.run --model catalog/my-model.yaml --prompt-set v2026-02-01 --seed 0,1,2 --output results/my-model-v1.json
- Generate quant profile (example, internal tool): ./tools/quantize --input model.pt --profile gptq-4bit --out model.quant.pt --calib-set=calib/1000.jsonl
- Compare outputs: python tools/token_diff.py --gold baseline.json --candidate results/my-model-v1.json --out diffs/my-model-diff.tsv
